transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. As you're aware, we have an anonymous report alleging that a procurement vice president steered technology purchases toward a preferred supplier. The preliminary review has looked at the procurement policy, selected emails, and payment records but hasn't reached a final conclusion. The audit committee is expecting my recommended resolution plan this Friday. Before I can present anything, I need to get a final check from investigations, finance, employment, and insurance counsel — that's our standard practice. I'd like to hear from each of you on where things stand so we can coordinate and make sure I'm in a position to present a sound recommendation on Friday.
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Elena, I need to update the group on where the investigations side stands. After conducting two additional witness interviews this week, I've concluded that the procurement vice president did steer the purchases in violation of company policy. I have not yet finalized that conclusion in the preliminary review memorandum, but based on what I've gathered, the allegation is substantiated. I wanted to make sure everyone here has that information as we coordinate toward Friday's presentation.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share a critical piece of information from the finance side. Yesterday, I reconciled the supplier invoices against the approved purchase orders for the transactions under review, and I can confirm that the company overpaid exactly $240,000 on those transactions. This reconciliation was completed yesterday and is not yet reflected in the preliminary review packet. This is a quantified financial impact that the audit committee will likely want to see in the resolution plan on Friday.

transcript.text: I need to share something from the employment side. In a confidential meeting this week, the reporting employee told me that the vice president had begun excluding them from meetings after the report was made. This is a retaliation concern that needs to be addressed. My required protective plan is anti-retaliation monitoring with check-ins every 14 days for exactly 60 days. I have not yet added this plan to the investigation file, but it needs to be included before Friday's presentation to the audit committee.

transcript.text: I need to flag something critical from the insurance side. I've reviewed our D&O policy, and the circumstances must be reported to the insurer within exactly 10 business days after becoming reasonably likely to produce a claim. Today is business day 6 since that threshold was met, and I have not yet circulated my policy review to the investigation team. If we don't provide notice within the 10-business-day window, we risk losing coverage for any claim that may arise from this matter. I recommend we make the insurer notification a tracked action item in the resolution plan for Friday, and I'll get my policy review circulated to all of you today.
